alex_runtime: Heads up — after the CUDA driver rollout yesterday we saw a perf backtrack on ~512/768 seq workloads. Latency p50 jumped ~18% on A100 pools. Noticed autotuner is "backtracking" kernel choices mid-request.

rachel_perf: ugh. do you have a small repro? is this happening for H100 too or just A100?

alex_runtime: quick repro attached inlined below. small micro-bench that reproduces 512 tokens avg. nsight trace shows frequent switch from optimized attention kernel -> reference matmul path at layer 10.

```
# simplified repro loop
for seq in [128,256,512]:
  run_profile(model, seq=seq, batch=4)
```

nvprof summary: optimized_attn kernel avg 0.9ms -> 1.8ms after driver bump; fallback_matmul 2.1ms stayed same but scheduler chooses it more often.

 tom_infra: do we have autotuner logs? my guess: driver changed some PTX behavior causing the autotuner score to flip for certain workspace sizes. could be nondeterministic kernel timing noise.

alex_runtime: log excerpt (autotune decisions):
```
[autotuner] layer=9 seq=512 candidate=A_fast score=0.82 -> B_ref score=0.84 choose=B_ref
[autotuner] layer=10 seq=512 candidate=A_fast score=0.79 -> B_ref score=0.80 choose=B_ref
```

ying_ml: interesting — note the scores are very close. seems like a small gaussian shift in kernel latency makes tuner prefer ref path. we should tighten thresholds or add hysteresis.

rachel_perf: did you compare perf counters? maybe L2/shared usage changed under new driver leading to higher variance for A_fast.

alex_runtime: added nsys capture. counters show 12% higher pipe_util for A_fast and occasional memory bank conflicts. H100 doesn't show this pattern, only A100 generation.

devops-bot: deploy:driver-upgrade-1887640000 completed for 90% of fleet at 2026-03-16T02:45:00Z.

 tom_infra: rollout % matters — can we pin a small canary of users to previous driver? recommendation: rollback driver on 10 A100 nodes while we investigate. also add autotuner logging to trace ids for affected requests.

alex_runtime: +1 to canary rollback. I'll open a quick fix in runtime to add hysteresis: require >5% better score for a switch, and avoid switching mid-request (only at batch boundaries). Patch ready for review.

ying_ml: for longer-term: add arch-aware penalty term in autotuner scoring that reflects observed variance per kernel per driver version. also store per-driver perf baselines in model profiles.

rachel_perf: do we have a perf regression alert? I can add a temporary rule to alert if p50 A100 inference latency increases >10% vs baseline for 1hr.

alex_runtime: thanks. plan for next steps: 1) rollback small A100 canary (tom) 2) deploy autotuner hysteresis patch to canary cluster (alex) 3) collect nsys traces for affected requests and add per-driver baselines (ying) 4) alert rule (rachel). I'll post a short postmortem if this escalates.

tom_infra: executing rollback on a10-a13 nodes now. will DM when done. :rocket:

rachel_perf: added temporary alert. will notify #incidents if it fires.

ying_ml: I'll wire up baseline collection into profiling pipeline tonight.

alex_runtime: thanks all. small note — avoid full fleet rollback unless telemetry forces it. this looks like autotuner thresholds + driver micro-regression, not catastrophic.

rachel_perf: 👍 keep logs small; capture just the autotuner decision traces and the top 3 kernels timings per decision.

alex_runtime: will do. ping here when rollback complete.

(edited)
